Principal Scientific Adviser to the Government of India, Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Launches Digital Platform to Optimise Waste Management in Cities
articles.full_content:
Prof. Ajay Kumar Sood, Principal Scientific Adviser (PSA) to the Government of India, chaired a meeting on 16 September 2026 to review the outcomes and recommendations of the project ‘Development of LCA Framework for Solid Waste Management (SWM) Technologies in India’. Dr Parvinder Maini, Scientific Secretary, also graced the meeting, which brought together Dr Vishal Chaudhary, Scientist ‘F’; Dr Hafsa Ahmad, Scientist ‘D’, from the Office of the PSA; Ms. Shravanthi, Deputy Adviser, Central Public Health and Environmental Engineering Organisation, Ministry of Housing and Urban Affairs; and Prof. M.S. Mohan Kumar, Prof. (Retd.), Department of Civil Engineering, IISc Bengaluru and Chair, Project Review Monitoring Committee. The project consortium included Prof. Lakshminarayana Rao and Prof. Chanakya Hoysall from IISc Bengaluru, Prof. R. Vinu from IIT Madras, and Prof. R. S. Singh from IIT (BHU) Varanasi, along with key research associates responsible for LCA modelling, GHG accounting, and digital tool development. Representatives from invited Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) also joined the meeting virtually.
Aligned with the vision of national missions like the Waste to Wealth Mission and the Swachh Bharat Mission-Urban, the Office of the PSA supported the project in 2024, which was jointly undertaken by IISc Bengaluru, IIT Madras, and IIT (BHU) Varanasi. It sought to develop a contextual and nationally relevant Life Cycle Assessment (LCA) framework, along with a GHG calculator web application, to help ULBs plan, compare, and optimise solid waste management systems with lower carbon footprints.
The project team presented findings from the LCA study covering a wide range of waste management technologies, supported by case studies from Bengaluru, Mysuru, Tumakuru, Chennai, Delhi, and Varanasi. A demonstration video of the GHG calculator app showcased its key features and how it can help ULBs quantify emissions associated with different SWM technologies and operating scenarios. The team also presented scenario comparison modules for evaluating alternative waste management pathways and identifying low-carbon options, along with detailed LCA insights into Indian SWM technologies such as biomining, anaerobic digestion, waste-to-energy, and landfilling.
The GHH calculator app developed under this project supports and enables the following-
• The user-friendly GHG calculator app designed specifically for Urban Local Bodies (ULBs) seamlessly analyses emissions from existing solid waste management practices.
• The app features common waste management processes like anaerobic digestion, incineration (waste-to-energy), composting, recycling and landfilling
• The app provides net emissions, avoided emissions, logistic emissions, carbon footprint, different GHG emission data (methane, carbondioxide, NOx, black carbon)
• The app helps the ULBs to visualize different best practice waste management scenarios that result in minimum GHG emissions with the lowest carbon foot

Ministry of Finance to organise a Conference of State Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat” on 18th and 19th Sept. 2026 in New Delhi
articles.full_content:
The Ministry of Finance will organise a Conference of Finance Ministers and Finance Secretaries of States and Union Territories with Legislature on “Financing India’s Journey towards Viksit Bharat ” on 18 th and 19 th Sept. 2026, in New Delhi. The Union Minister for Finance & Corporate Affairs will be present during the conference. Several Chief Ministers and Finance Ministers from the States will participate along with senior State officials in the conference.
The Conference on Financing India’s Journey Towards Viksit Bharat will be on the policy complementarities between the Centre and the States, and will bring together academic rigour and practical policy to deliberate on financing challenges and policy priorities for India’s development journey.
Smt. Anuradha Thakur, Secretary, Department of Economic Affairs (DEA), Ministry of Finance, will briefly highlight the objectives of the conference at the inaugural session.
The keynote address at the inaugural session will be delivered by Shri N.K. Singh, President and Life Trustee, Institute of Economic Growth, and Chairman, 15 th Finance Commission (XVFC). Shri Sudhir Shrivastava, former Additional Chief Secretary and Finance Secretary, Government of Maharashtra, will present the State’s perspective on financing Viksit Bharat .
The conference will have three thematic sessions:
• Macroeconomic overview
• Financing agricultural transformation
• Financing the energy transition
Providing the context for these two-hour deliberations are background papers that have been circulated to the participants on topics such as macroeconomic milestones and pathways towards Viksit Bharat , Private financing for Viksit Bharat , Implications of GST 2.0 for States; Financing agricultural markets and marketing, Financing resilience and sustainable resource use in Indian agriculture; Financing renewable energy and transmission assets, and Financing carbon capture utilisation and storage, among others.
Additionally, Dr. Saurabh Garg, Secretary, Ministry of Statistics and Programme Implementation (MoSPI), will highlight importance of measuring growth outcomes in India’s journey towards Viksit Bharat ; and Shri S. Krishnan, Secretary, Ministry of Electronics and Information Technology (MeitY), will briefly highlight the role of new-age technology in good governance.

articles.full_content:
Third Anniversary of PM Vishwakarma to be Celebrated in Kolkata on 17th September 2026 Union Minister Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi and Chief Minister of West Bengal Shri Suvendu Adhikari to Grace the Celebrations
The Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India, will celebrate the Third Anniversary of the PM Vishwakarma Scheme on 17th September 2026 at the Dhono Dhanyo Auditorium, Kolkata, West Bengal. The event will mark three years of the implementation of the Scheme aimed at providing comprehensive and end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople and strengthening their livelihoods and entrepreneurial capabilities.
Shri Jitan Ram Manjhi, Union Minister for MSME, Government of India, along with Shri Suvendu Adhikari, Chief Minister of West Bengal, will grace the occasion in the august presence of Sushri Shobha Karandlaje, Minister of State for MSME, Government of India. Shri Dipak Barman, Minister-in-Charge, Department of Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises & Textiles (MSME&T), Government of West Bengal, and Shri Ashok Dinda, Minister of State for Micro, Small and Medium Enterprises and Textiles, Government of West Bengal, will also grace the event.
Senior officials from the Ministry of MSME, Government of India, including representatives of the Office of the Development Commissioner (MSME), Khadi and Village Industries Commission (KVIC), National Small Industries Corporation (NSIC), State Level Bankers’ Committee (SLBC), and India Post, will also participate in the event.
The event will be attended by PM Vishwakarma beneficiaries, representatives of Gram Panchayats/Urban Local Bodies (ULBs), Common Service Centres (CSCs)/Village Level Entrepreneurs (VLEs), and other stakeholders. An exhibition featuring various stalls showcasing products of local artisans and craftspeople will also be organised, providing them with a platform for the display and sale of their products.
Three Years of PM Vishwakarma
The PM Vishwakarma Scheme was launched by the Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi on 17th September 2023 with the objective of providing end-to-end support to traditional artisans and craftspeople engaged in 18 identified trades. The Scheme seeks to strengthen the traditional skills of Vishwakarmas by providing them with institutional support, modern tools, access to finance, skill upgradation and market linkages, thereby enabling them to enhance their productivity, income and entrepreneurial potential.
The Scheme provides a comprehensive package of support comprising recognition through PM Vishwakarma certificates and identity cards, skill upgradation, toolkit incentive, credit support, incentives for digital transactions and marketing support.
In a significant milestone achieved within three years of its launch, 30 lakh beneficiaries have been registered under the PM Vishwakarma Scheme after completion of the prescribed three-stage verification process, thereby achieving the registration target under the Scheme.

Union Minister of State Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh launches India’s Net Zero Portal and NAPCC Dashboard on World Ozone Day 2026
articles.full_content:
Digital platforms to promote Voluntary Net Zero Action and Strengthen Monitoring of National Climate Missions
Union Minister of State for Environment, Forest and Climate Change, Shri Kirti Vardhan Singh, today launched India’s Net Zero Portal and the National Action Plan on Climate Change (NAPCC) Dashboard on the occasion of World Ozone Day 2026 in Mumbai. The two digital initiatives mark an important step towards strengthening transparency, coordination and evidence-based climate action. The Net Zero Portal provides a national platform for voluntary Net Zero commitments by entities, while the NAPCC Dashboard enables consolidated monitoring of progress across the National Missions on climate change.
A significant step towards India’s #NetZero journey! On #WorldOzoneDay , HMoS Shri @KVSinghMPGonda launched India’s Net Zero Portal - a centralised digital platform for voluntary registration and disclosure of Net Zero commitments by Indian entities across sectors. (1/2) pic.twitter.com/F4G9683pN4
The Net Zero Portal is a centralised digital platform for voluntary registration and disclosure of Net Zero commitments by Indian entities across sectors. Participating entities can disclose their greenhouse gas (GHG) emissions, declare Net Zero targets and provide annual progress updates. Entities are encouraged to report Scope 1 and Scope 2 emissions, while reporting of Scope 3 emissions remains voluntary. The Portal also enables entities to outline pathways towards Net Zero, including measures related to clean energy transition, energy efficiency, technological interventions and carbon removals, as applicable.
The initiative brings voluntary climate actions onto a common platform, enhances transparency and encourages credible long-term climate planning. Entities successfully declaring their Net Zero targets will receive an acknowledgement from the MoEFCC. Public access to declarations by participating entities, organisations and industries will also create a consolidated repository of voluntary Net Zero actions in the country. The Portal can be accessed at: https://netzeroindia.moef.gov.in/
The NAPCC Dashboard provides a consolidated digital view of implementation and progress across the National Missions under the NAPCC. It brings together mission-related information and identified indicators on a common platform, facilitating systematic monitoring by concerned Ministries and Departments. The Dashboard will strengthen inter-ministerial coordination, support evidence-based assessment of national climate actions, help assess sectoral progress, identify implementation gaps and consolidate relevant inputs from Ministries and Departments. It is also expected to strengthen the linkages between domestic climate actions and India’s international climate commitments. The Dashboard can be accessed at: https://napccindia.moef.gov.in/
The launch of the Net Zero Portal and NAPCC Dashboard reflects the Government of India’s continued emphasis on technology-enabled gov

PM Vishwakarma: Strengthening Traditional Artisans and Craftspeople
articles.full_content:
As PM Vishwakarma approaches three years, its registration target of 30 lakh beneficiaries has been achieved. The scheme has also delivered skill training, toolkits, credit support, digital incentives and market linkages. Beneficiaries are also being onboarded on the Udyam Assist Platform and connected with wider market channels, including GeM, e-commerce platforms, trade fairs and exhibitions. The scheme is built around Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi and also seeks to strengthen the Guru-Shishya parampara and family-based practice of traditional skills.
Supporting Traditional Artisans and Craftspeople
India’s traditional artisans and craftspeople form an important part of the country’s local economy and cultural heritage. Many of these occupations depend on manual skills, family-based knowledge and small-scale enterprise. PM Vishwakarma was launched on 17 September 2023 to provide end-to-end support to such artisans and craftspeople .
PM Vishwakarma is built around the three pillars of Samman, Samarthya and Samriddhi, reflecting respect, capability and prosperity for traditional artisans and craftspeople. The scheme also seeks to strengthen and nurture the Guru-Shishya parampara or family-based practice of traditional skills.
The Central Sector Scheme has an outlay of ₹13,000 crore for FY2023-24 to FY2027-28, covering 18 traditional trades. The scheme seeks to improve the quality and reach of artisans’ products and services and facilitate their integration with domestic and global supply chain.
As the scheme approaches 3 years on 17 September 2026, its registration target of 30 lakh beneficiaries has already been achieved .
Scheme Framework and Key Components
PM Vishwakarma brings multiple forms of support within one framework. Its major components are recognition, skill upgradation, toolkit incentive, credit support, incentive for digital transactions and marketing support.
• On completion of the registration and verification process, beneficiaries are provided recognition through a PM Vishwakarma Certificate and ID Card .
Skill Upgradation
• Through skill upgradation, beneficiaries are introduced to modern tools, best practices and innovative designs . Training also covers digital transactions, marketing and entrepreneurial knowledge.
• Basic Training runs for 5–7 days, while Advanced Training is for 15 days or more. Trainees receive a stipend of ₹500 per day.
Modern toolkits of up to ₹15,000 are also provided to the eligible beneficiaries of the Scheme.
Access to formal credit is a central part of PM Vishwakarma. The scheme provides collateral-free Enterprise Development Loans of up to ₹3 lakh in two tranches. The first tranche is up to ₹1 lakh with an 18-month tenure. Beneficiaries completing Basic Training are eligible for the first tranche of loan. The second is up to ₹2 lakh with a 30-month tenure.

He stated that the true impact of the event lies in the collaborations on the ground for Circular Solutions and stressed on the need to move forward together from commitment to action. The Minister highlighted that the circular economy is not merely an environmental agenda but an economic opportunity, a societal responsibility, a daily lifestyle, and a pathway to secure a sustainable future for generations to come.

Circular economy is not an environmental issue but an economic and developmental opportunity, which is no longer a future possibility but one that is already prevalent globally. She noted that the importance of inclusion and peoples’ dimension of transition have been specifically highlighted during WCEF2026, besides exploring practical partnerships, business collaborations, innovations and investments in circular solutions. Ideas must become investments and successful innovations must scale with faster implementation, she concluded.

articles.full_content:
Shri Ashok Kumar Lahiri, Vice-Chairman, NITI Aayog, released the latest edition of the “ Trade Watch Quarterly ” publication for Quarter 1 of FY27 (Apr-Jun 2026) on 16 th September 2026, in New Delhi alongwith CEO and other senior officials of NITI Aayog.
The latest edition of Trade Watch Quarterly provides a comprehensive assessment of global and domestic trade trends amid heightened geopolitical and trade policy uncertainties, even as global trade has remained resilient. Global goods trade reached $13.7 trillion in the first half of calendar year 2026 , registering 12.5% y-o-y growth , while services trade expanded by 10.5% . Against this backdrop, India’s merchandise and services trade continued to expand, with total trade reaching $506.9 billion in Q1 FY27 , registering 15.5% y-o-y growth . The thematic focus of this edition is India’s metals and ores trade , a strategically important sector for manufacturing, infrastructure, energy transition and advanced industries. The study examines India’s export competitiveness and growing import dependence across metals and ores, with a focus on critical minerals and higher-value non-ferrous metals, while assessing structural constraints and opportunities to strengthen domestic value addition, investment, market diversification and global competitiveness.
India’s merchandise exports grew strongly in Q1 FY27, led by mineral fuels, electrical machinery, nuclear reactors, iron and steel, and vehicles, supported by rise in shipments of petroleum products, steel, engineering goods and automobiles. Imports continued to support India’s industrial and energy requirements, with notable growth in capital goods, electronic components and copper. This trend reflects the strength of domestic investment activity, expanding industrial capacity and the growing integration of Indian industry with global value chains.
India’s export destinations continued to diversify, with Tanzania and South Africa emerging among the top ten markets, alongside strong growth in exports to Singapore. Imports from Latin America and West Africa recorded significant growth, supported in part by the diversification of crude oil sourcing, thereby enhancing resilience and flexibility in India’s import basket. At the same time, Northeast Asia, West Asia-GCC and ASEAN remained important sources of imports, together accounting for around half of India’s total imports. Trade with FTA partners also gained further momentum, with exports increasing by 36.3% and imports by 10.0%, underscoring the strengthening of economic partnerships and deeper integration of India with global trade and supply chains.
India’s position in Digitally Delivered Services (DDS) also strengthened, with exports rising from $277 billion in 2024 to $317 billion in 2025, a 15% y-o-y increase. India consequently moved from the fifth-largest to the fourth-largest DDS exporter, only behind the US, UK and Ireland.

Building on Special Campaign 5.0 Achievements, Ministry of Mines Strengthens e-Waste Management under Special Campaign 6.0
articles.full_content:
The Government of India has decided to launch Special Campaign 6.0 from 2 nd October -31 October, 2026. Building upon the achievements of Special Campaign 5.0, this year, the Ministry is preparing for Special Campaign 6.0 , with focus area as “Effective Collection, Segregation and Disposal of e-Waste” in keeping with the Government’s commitment to swachhata, sustainability and responsible resource management.
Building on the success of special campaign 5.0 and continued efforts thereafter from November 2025 to August 2026 , the Ministry and its field organizations have recorded significant progress towards improving administrative efficiency and ensuring optimum utilisation of government resources.
During this period, a total of 1,772 public grievances were addressed and 3,751 physical files were weeded out , contributing to improved record management and streamlined administrative processes. The campaign also resulted in the freeing of more than 1.7 lakh sq. ft. of office space , enabling more effective utilisation of government premises. In addition, 116 campaigns were undertaken across the Ministry and its organisations, resulting in revenue generation of approximately Rs. 19.33 crore through scrap disposal.
As part of Special Campaign 6.0 , the Preparatory Phase from 15th to 30th September 2026 will focus on identifying and setting targets for the disposal of pending references from MPs, the PMO and State Governments, Public grievances and appeals, Parliamentary assurances , as well as the review and management of records.
The Implementation Phase from 2nd to 31st October 2026 will focus on achieving the identified targets through coordinated efforts of the Ministry of Mines, its attached and subordinate offices, CPSEs and autonomous bodies.
In line with this year’s theme, the Ministry has nominated JNARDDC, an autonomous body under the Ministry, which in collaboration with MRAI, will facilitate the setting up of e-Waste collection booths at GPOA and various offices of the Ministry of Mines, as well as at government offices across different States and locations, for the collection of e-Waste. The initiative is aimed at facilitating the recycling and recovery of critical minerals from e-Waste, which is line with the objectives of the National Critical Mineral Mission (NCMM).
Through Special Campaign 6.0, the Ministry of Mines will continue to strengthen its efforts towards swachhata, sustainability, efficient governance and responsible resource management , while contributing to the broader national objective of sustainable development
The campaign will reinforce the Ministry’s endeavour to institutionalise efficient practices in government offices and promote environmentally responsible management of resources, including e-Waste.

Shri Rajiv Gauba Calls Electric Mobility a "Strategic Imperative" for Viksit Bharat as NITI Aayog Launches Second Edition of India Electric Mobility Index
articles.full_content:
Shri Rajiv Gauba, in his address at the NITI Aayog Workshop on State EV Policies, where the second edition of the India Electric Mobility Index (IEMI) report was launched, highlighted that the global transition to electric mobility is well underway.
In 2025, he noted, electric cars accounted for around one-tenth of new car sales in the US, more than a quarter in the EU, and over half in China and that these shares are expected to rise significantly across the world in the years ahead. He pointed to the recent West Asia crisis, noting that it could become a major inflection point for electric mobility, much as the oil crises of the 1970s accelerated the global push towards greater fuel efficiency.
Describing the shift as “an economic, environmental, and strategic imperative” for the Viksit Bharat 2047 vision, he highlighted India’s dependence on imports for nearly 89% of its crude oil requirements, a dependence that is likely to increase as car ownership rises from current levels if EVs are not adopted more widely. He noted that the automotive sector contributes around 7.1% of GDP and supports nearly 1.9 crore jobs, underscoring the importance of keeping the sector aligned with the global transition to electric vehicles. He also highlighted the significant public health costs of vehicular emissions in cities such as Delhi, making the transition to cleaner mobility an urgent priority.
He outlined the scale of government support already in place, totalling over ₹92,000 crore, through schemes such as FAME, PM E-DRIVE and PM E-bus Sewa, as well as two production-linked incentive schemes for Automobiles & Auto Components and for Advanced Chemistry Cell battery storage.
He also highlighted the rapid expansion of the EV charging ecosystem, with oil marketing companies and private players driving the development of charging infrastructure. The newly launched Unified Bharat e-Charge app is expected to further strengthen this ecosystem by making charging infrastructure more accessible and convenient for users.
Turning to States, he noted that 29 of India's 36 States and Union Territories have now notified EV policies, with IEMI scores showing broad-based improvement; the highest State score rising from 77 to 84 and the median score from 36 to 40 over the past year.
He noted that the Index offers a data-driven framework to help states monitor their progress and formulate evidence-based policies. He also emphasized that the differences between States experience in E-Mobility due to differing strategies, shaped by their own industrial base, fiscal capacity and geography are not a complication, but a strength, provided states learn from each other. He urged States to prioritise electrifying public transport in select cities, ensure charging infrastructure is spatially well-distributed and reliable, and promote investments in research and innovation.

articles.full_content:
Gram Panchayat-level annual digital self-assessment framework for assessment of rural sanitation service delivery Gram Sabha validation to strengthen community participation, transparency and accountability
Union Minister of Jal Shakti, Shri C R Patil launched Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) on 15 th September 2026 during a virtual meeting with States/UTs. The meeting was attended by the Hon’ble Minister of State for Jal Shakti, Shri V. Somanna. Ministers in charge of Rural Sanitation and concerned officials and Mission Directors of Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) from States/UTs joined virtually.
Swachh Seva Aankalan (SSA) is an annual, Gram Panchayat level digital self-assessment framework developed by Department of Drinking Water and Sanitation under Swachh Bharat Mission (Grameen) 2.0 for assessment and monitoring of sanitation service delivery in rural areas. This multi-tier evaluation framework envisages the involvement of Gram Panchayats, Gram Sabhas, Village Water & Sanitation Committees (VWSC), District and State/UT level officials for strengthening sanitation service delivery at grass root level.
Under SSA, ODF Plus (Model) declared Gram Panchayats, together with their VWSCs and local communities, will assess the status of ODF sustainability, visual cleanliness and Solid and Liquid Waste Management (SLWM) in the Gram Panchayat. The functionality and Operation & Maintenance (O&M) status of sanitation and community SLWM assets will also be self-assessed through the Aankalan. The findings will be discussed and validated by the concerned Gram Sabha and will be available to the District and State/UT authorities to be reviewed in DWSM/SWSM meetings. These authorities will be able to identify service delivery gaps and prepare their respective improvement plans for corrective action at grassroot level.
In the spirit of the 73 rd Constitutional Amendment Act, this will further empower the Gram Panchayats and Gram Sabhas to review their achievements and progress and make focused efforts for improvement in the same.

A delegation of senior journalists from Chandigarh visited the Central Tool Room & Training Centre (CTTC), Bhubaneswar, today on an exposure tour coordinated by the Press Information Bureau (PIB), Bhubaneswar. The visit aimed to provide the media fraternity with comprehensive insight into the pioneering achievements and operational excellence of this premier institute functioning under the Ministry of Micro, Small & Medium Enterprises (MSME), Government of India. The delegation was accompanied by Shri Pritam Singh, Director, PIB Chandigarh; Shri Partha Sarathi Malik, Assistant Director, PIB Bhubaneswar; and Shri Dharam Singh from PIB Chandigarh.
Welcoming the delegates, Dr. K. M. Rajan, General Manager In-charge, CTTC Bhubaneswar, delivered a presentation outlining the Centre’s pivotal role in bolstering the nation’s precision manufacturing capabilities and technical skill ecosystem. He spotlighted CTTC’s strategic support to critical aerospace initiatives, notably with the Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO), alongside its industry-aligned training curriculum designed to bridge the academia-industry gap.
During an extensive walkthrough of the production and specialized training divisions, the journalists witnessed the Centre's state-of-the-art infrastructure. The tour encompassed advanced additive manufacturing facilities featuring 3D metal and plastic printing, cutting-edge Industry 4.0, Robotics, and IoT laboratories, alongside high-precision CNC milling and turning blocks. The delegation also observed the massive digital design ecosystem comprising over 4,000 workstations equipped with modern CAD/CAM suites.
Interacting with students engaged in live operations, the media team commended the high level of practical competence demonstrated by the trainees. The visiting journalists observed that replicating such world-class infrastructure and pedagogical standards across different states would substantially empower the nation's youth, accelerating India's competitiveness in the global manufacturing landscape.
Shri Susanta Kumar Rout, Head of Administration, Accounts & HR, CTTC Bhubaneswar, conveyed his gratitude to the media delegation. He underscored the media's vital role in amplifying public awareness regarding advanced technical skilling and high-precision engineering among the youth. The visit concluded with an interactive exchange that reinforced the collaborative bridge between the media and key national institutes driving technological self-reliance and industrial progress.

articles.full_content:

A National Webinar on Solid and e-Waste Management was organised today in New Delhi, by the Department of School Education & Literacy (DoSEL), Union Ministry of Education, as a lead-up to Swachhata Hi Seva 2026 and Special Campaign 6.0.
Secretary, DoSEL, Shri T. K. Anil Kumar, highlighted the vision of National Education Policy (NEP) 2020 towards inculcating environmental awareness and responsible citizenship among school students. He informed that under Special Campaign 5.0, around one lakh school students collected over 4,000 kgs of e-waste, across 10 cities in four States and one Union Territory. He added that effective implementation of the Solid Waste Management Rules 2026 was essential for reducing pollution, conserving resources, promoting recycling and resource recovery and ensuring the safe and scientific management of waste.
Joint Secretary, DoSEL, Dr. Amarpreet Duggal, highlighted the pivotal role of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE in providing a valuable platform for students to understand environmental challenges and develop environmentally responsible attitudes, values and behaviour. She said that the convergence of Swachhata Pakhwada (September 1 to 15, 2026), Swachhata Hi Seva (September 17 - October 17, 2026) and Special Campaign 6.0 (October 2 to 31, 2026), should be seen as an opportunity to deepen the culture of cleanliness and responsible environmental practices among school students and the wider school community.
As part of Swachhata Hi Seva 2026, she also announced a Quiz Competition on “Solid Waste Management Rules 2026” for students from Grades 6 th to 12 th . The quiz will be hosted on the Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE portal from September 17 to October 17, 2026: https://ecoclubs.education.gov.in/swachhata-hi-seva?start=quiz
The Webinar featured expert presentations on ‘Solid Waste Management’ and a walkthrough of the portal of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, providing participants with an overview of the digital platform and its resources for environmental awareness and student engagement.
Held under the aegis of Eco Clubs for Mission LiFE, the Webinar was aimed at sensitising school students and stakeholders on responsible waste management practices, source segregation, recycling, reuse and safe disposal of solid and electronic waste. More than 2.6 lakh school students, teachers and community members on YouTube participated in the Webinar.
A Portal for Special Campaign 6.0 was also launched today in another event. Speaking on the occasion, Secretary, DoSEL, informed that the Department had set a target of undertaking 7 lakh cleanliness campaigns across the country under Special Campaign 6.0.

Union Minister for Environment, Forest and Climate Change Shri Bhupender Yadav, along with Chief Minister (Gujarat), Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel, inaugurated the World Circular Economy Forum 2026 at Gandhinagar today. The forum is being organised under the theme 'Circular Economy: Transition for People and Prosperity', from 15th - 18th September . Other dignitaries gracing the inaugural session included Minister for Forest, Environment and Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Arjunbhai Modhwadia; Minister of State for Forests and Environment, Climate Change (Gujarat), Shri Pravinbhai Mali; Ambassador of Finland to India, Ambassador of Finland to India, H.E. Mr. Mikko Kivikoski; Dy. Directoe General (Circular Economy), Ministry of Economic Affairs and Climate (Netherlands), Ms. Marieke Spijkerboer; President SITRA, Mr. Atte Jääskeläinen, along with senior officials from the Government of India and Government of Gujarat.
In his special address, Shri Bhupendrabhai Patel said the first-ever hosting of WCEF in South Asia reflects India’s growing global leadership under the vision of Prime Minister Shri Narendra Modi. He said Mission LiFE is emerging as a foundation for the global circular economy and expressed confidence that the Forum would showcase practical circular economy practices for the world.
The Chief Minister reflected on Gujarat’s journey towards environmental conservation, while maintaining a balance between development and the environment. Highlighting traditional circular practices, he cited the example of offerings at the Somnath Temple being recycled into reusable resources and generating livelihoods for local communities. He emphasised that the culture of reuse and the concept of converting waste into wealth have long been part of Indian traditions, and called for WCEF to embody the spirit of Vasudhaiva Kutumbakam by developing practical circular solutions for the world.
In his keynote address on the occasion, Shri Bhupender Yadav said that for India, the circular economy is “not a new destination; it is a new way of looking at an old wisdom”. He said the principles of reuse, repair and respect for resources have been deeply embedded in India’s social and cultural fabric. “What we now describe in policy language as circularity was once simply common sense in everyday Indian life - repair before replace, reuse before discard, and recover before waste”, he stated. The Minister said the choice is not between growth and the environment, but an opportunity to make growth itself more resource-efficient, resilient

The Periodic Labour Force Survey (PLFS) conducted by NSO, MoSPI, is the primary source of data on activity participation and employment and unemployment conditions of the population. The PLFS survey methodology has been modified from January, 2025 to provide monthly and quarterly estimates of labour force indicators for the country.
Monthly results of PLFS are released in the form of Monthly Bulletins. It presents estimates of key labour market indicators viz. Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR), Worker Population Ratio (WPR) and Unemployment Rate (UR) at the all-India level following the Current Weekly Status[1] (CWS) approach.
The Monthly Bulletins for April, 2025 to July, 2026 have already been released. The present Monthly Bulletin for August, 2026 is the seventeenth in the series.

• Labour Force Participation Rate (LFPR) strengthened:

In urban areas, LFPR remained constant at 50.4% in August, 2026 as compared to the previous month.
